text: The Ruby in the Smoke is a mystery novel for young adults written by English author Philip Pullman and first published in 1985. Set in the Victorian era, the story follows 16-year-old Sally Lockhart as she uncovers the cause of her father's mysterious death. The book won the 1987 Lancashire Children's Book of the Year Award and is the first in the Sally Lockhart Quartet, which includes The Shadow in the North, The Tiger in the Well, and The Tin Princess. It was adapted for television in 2006, with a TV film written by Adrian Hodges and starring Billie Piper, produced by the BBC and aired on BBC One on 27 December 2006 and on PBS's Masterpiece Mystery! as The Sally Lockhart Mysteries: The Ruby in the Smoke on 4 February 2007, attracting 7.07 million UK viewers. This adaptation marked the television debut of actor Matt Smith, who later became the Eleventh Doctor in Doctor Who, a series in which Billie Piper had previously appeared. All four Sally Lockhart books were expected to be adapted for television; as of December 2025, no adaptation of The Tiger in the Well has been announced. In August 2016, a stage adaptation written and directed by Madeleine Perham premiered at The Pleasance during the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, receiving Pullman's blessing. The production, which ran for one month in the King Dome venue, was critically acclaimed, with The Scotsman calling it "a compelling tale, and full of surprises, moral ambiguities and people who are other than they seem," and Jane Berg from Three Weeks awarding it five stars, stating it was "one of the most enjoyable hours I've spent at this festival." Broadway Baby rated it four stars, noting it "delighted in its Victorian setting" and was "an excellent piece of storytelling." The stage show was created by Reprint Productions (now Escapade), featuring a cast of six who multi-roled the various characters: Rebecca Lenihan, Sydney Austin, Tris Hobson, Martin Coates, Hamish Forbes, and Madeleine Golding, who also served as producer and co-founder of Reprint.
